review.tagline: Self-hostable backend with auth, databases, storage, functions, messaging and hosting
review.summary: Appwrite is a backend platform that bundles Auth, Databases, Storage, Functions, Sites, Messaging, Realtime and a Firewall behind REST, GraphQL and WebSocket APIs. It runs as a managed cloud or self-hosted via a Docker installer, and offers a hosted MCP server so coding agents can operate on a live project. Client and server SDKs cover Web, Flutter, Apple, Android, React Native, Unity, Node.js, Python, PHP, Go, Rust and others.
review.audience: Developers who want a self-hosted or managed backend for web and mobile apps
strengths: One Docker-based installer sets up the full stack, with Compose and env files also published
SDKs for 6 client and 10 server platforms, plus REST, GraphQL and Realtime APIs
Hosted MCP server uses OAuth, so no API keys are needed on Cloud
Same product runs on managed Cloud or on your own infrastructure
weaknesses: Installer needs access to the Docker socket on the host
Self-hosted instances must use a separate local MCP server, not the hosted one
Hybrid monolith-plus-workers architecture means many services to operate
RAM and CPU requirements are not stated in the README
